observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a bare 4-cylinder engine block with intake manifold, coil packs, pulleys, alternator and oil cap visible.
No manufacturer badge, engine code, VIN sticker, or identification plate is legible in either photo.
A reseller watermark 'EMMY GOLD AUTO SPARE' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' appear across both images; this is the seller's branding, not proof of the engine's origin or condition.
Engine is shown sitting on a tiled floor/workshop area, not mounted or running; no video, sound, or compression test is shown.
No oil, coolant, or any fluid test is visible; no close-up of block stamp or casting numbers that would confirm Hyundai/Kia identity.

claims.evidence: No badge, casting mark, or ID tag readable in photo 0 or photo 1
No import documents, customs sticker, or shipping label shown in either photo
No video or audio clip of the engine running; photos show it static and disassembled from a vehicle
No mileage tag, odometer photo, or donor-vehicle documentation visible
Valve cover and block seams are not shown close enough to check for gasket disturbance or tool marks

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage despite 'tested' claim
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine running/idling with audible sound, plus compression test readout

risks.risk: Brand/model may not actually be Hyundai/Kia or may be a mismatched variant
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine block casting number or ID plate
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unverified 4-cylinder engine, not brand-specific

risks.risk: Mileage and import origin cannot be confirmed, common exaggeration in 'tokunbo' listings
risks.proof: Photo of Belgian customs/import paperwork or auction sheet
risks.if_unproven: priced without any low-mileage or genuine-import premium

risks.risk: Engine could have been opened/repaired and resealed
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all valve cover and block mating surfaces/bolts for tool marks or fresh gasket sealant

proof_requests: Video of the engine actually running, with audible sound, ideally showing oil pressure/temp gauges
Close-up photo of the engine block casting number or stamped ID code confirming Hyundai/Kia model
Photo of any import/customs documentation showing Belgium origin and mileage
Close-up of valve cover seams and bolts to check for prior disassembly
response.reason: The photos show a genuine bare 4-cylinder engine consistent with the seller's stated type, but none of the working, mileage, origin, or 'never opened' claims can be confirmed from the images, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, unproven-condition engine.
